clue.text: Bill is lost when Tabitha gets about island

indicators.note: the bill is lost from the name, so those letters are removed from it

parts.note: taken as written
a tab is a bill, as at a bar
CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A woman called Tabitha travels around an island and loses track of a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lost when' signals the bill coming out of the woman's name; 'gets' is only a link. Ithaca is Odysseus's home island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca is the Greek island home of Odysseus in Homer's epic.

clue.text: Tucked into sirloin steaks this month

indicators.note: tucked into means the letters are tucked inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into sirloin steaks this month.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters lie in sirloIN STeaks. INST is old letter-writing shorthand for instant, this month.
explanation.definitionFit: Inst., short for instant, is old business-letter shorthand for the current month.

clue.text: House share, mostly in Nelson

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the share word is dropped

parts.note: a ration is a share or allowance

explanation.surface: A house share is mostly found in Nelson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts N from RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio was the first name of Admiral Lord Nelson, the British naval hero.

clue.text: Sales technique that's uncaring, beginning to concern everyone

parts.note: cold means unfeeling or uncaring

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of concern is used

parts.note: all is everyone

explanation.surface: A sales technique seems uncaring and starts to worry everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsolicited sales approach to a stranger by phone or visit is this technique.

clue.text: Dreamer sailed about in it

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of sailed are moved around

explanation.surface: A dreamer goes sailing about in some vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sailed' tempts as a verb in the surface, but 'about' makes it the anagram fodder, and 'in' places the result inside the word it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer, someone pursuing perfect visions over practicality, is a synonym.

clue.text: Make unattractive and awkward men get ideas

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters are put into a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: Awkward men with ideas make themselves unappealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unattractive' is meant magnetically: removing magnetism means a thing no longer attracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing magnetism means an object stops attracting metal, punning on attractiveness.

clue.text: Skilful cobbler's last to get into trouble with it

indicators.note: to get into puts the letter inside the trouble word

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: last means the final letter of cobbler's is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A skilful shoemaker finishes his work and lands in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' gives R, the end of cobbler; 'to get into' puts it in ADO. A cobbler's last is also a shoe form, the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit is a synonym for skilful, deft with hands or mind.

clue.text: Endlessly abuse a Russian leader for being restricted in outlook

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the abuse word is dropped

parts.note: insult means abuse

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Russian is used

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded Russian leader is subjected to constant abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts T from INSULT; 'leader' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular means narrow-minded, as cut off as an island.

clue.text: Captain's heart in his place somewhere in Kent?

indicators.note: heart means the middle letter of captain is taken

parts.note: a ship's captain's place is on the bridge

explanation.surface: A captain is at home somewhere in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' gives T, the centre of capTain. KENT is a county in south-east England; Tonbridge is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a town in the English county of Kent, the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Confidently backing American bank

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for American is turned round

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: An American bank is confidently returning money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns US into SU; 'bank' is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is an adverb of certainty, saying something with confidence.

clue.text: Polite denial retracted after little devil has to shut up

indicators.note: after places the turned denial behind the devil in the answer

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: retracted means the polite denial is drawn back, read in reverse

parts.note: no sir is a polite way to refuse

explanation.surface: A child, the little devil, is shut away after politely denying something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retracted' turns the polite refusal round, and 'after' puts it behind the little devil; 'has to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to shut them up, locking them away.

clue.text: Pin that may be present

parts.note: a pin is slang for a leg, which fills a hosiery item; and a small gift tucked into a Christmas sock is the other reading

explanation.surface: A pin is offered as a possible gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin' is slang for leg: a leg fills a stocking, and a small present goes in a Christmas stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gift put into a Christmas sock is exactly this, and a leg literally fills hosiery.

clue.text: Bats flit in with friend of Badger or Mole?

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Ratty is Badger's friend in The Wind in the Willows
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bats flit about with the animal friends of Kenneth Grahame's riverbank tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' is the anagram signal, not the animal: FLIT IN becomes INFILT. Mole is the spy sense, not the Wind in the Willows animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy planted inside an organisation, an undercover agent.

clue.text: One may find shelf to rip off?

definitions.text: One may find shelf to rip off?

indicators.note: off, in the sense of gone wrong, signals the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A thief eyes a shop shelf to plunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SHELF TO RIP, and the whole clue describes such a thief, who rips off goods from a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A store thief steals goods from shelves, which is what ripping off a shelf means.

clue.text: Two garments required for baseball player

parts.note: shorts are a garment worn on the legs
a top is a garment worn on the upper body

explanation.surface: A baseball player needs two items of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both pieces: SHORTS and TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder positioned between second and third base in baseball has this name.

clue.text: Unfinished business in jazz

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: trade is business or commerce

explanation.surface: Some business in the jazz world remains incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts the E off TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is short for traditional jazz, the early New Orleans style.

clue.text: One may be found on the breakfast table, having urge to make love

definitions.text: One may be found on the breakfast table

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
to spoon is old slang for kissing and cuddling

explanation.surface: A lover at breakfast feels the urge for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: EGG as in egg on; SPOON is dated slang for courting.
explanation.definitionFit: A small utensil for eating boiled eggs lies on the breakfast table.

clue.text: Showing a bit of touchiness with a pained expression

indicators.note: a bit of means a short run of letters is taken from inside the word

explanation.surface: Someone shows a touchy streak and a pained look.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside tOUCHiness, signalled by 'a bit of'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of pain is a pained expression in the sense of an utterance.

clue.text: Company drudge upset contemporaries

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the drudge word is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a slave is a drudge

explanation.surface: A company's drudge annoys colleagues of the same age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SLAVE into EVALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Coevals are people of the same age or era, synonymous with contemporaries.

clue.text: Winged horse that may be executed in ring

definitions.meaning: a horse that flies, like Pegasus, read literally

definitions.text: that may be executed in ring
definitions.meaning: a wrestling throw over the shoulder, performed in the ring

explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling throw takes this name, and read literally it describes a horse that flies.

clue.text: Course isn't always written up

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

indicators.note: written up in a down clue means the word is set upwards

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: The course is not always recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns EER (e'er) into REE. AINTREE is the racecourse near Liverpool where the Grand National steeplechase is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous British racecourse, home of the Grand National horse race.

clue.text: Old Ford signs up

definitions.meaning: a car model made by Ford in the 1950s and 60s
the twelve astrological signs set up in the heavens

explanation.definitionFit: Ford made a car of this name, and it is the band of twelve star signs overhead.

clue.text: Noted work taking a whole year

definitions.meaning: a piece written in musical notes, Vivaldi's set of violin concertos
spring, summer, autumn and winter together span a year

explanation.definitionFit: Vivaldi's famous concertos bear this title, and the quarters of the calendar together make a full year.

clue.text: Dope left in bed

indicators.note: in places the left letter inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone doped is left lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope and a clot are both informal British words for a fool.

clue.text: Supporters of absolute rule making Tass stir?

indicators.note: making, with the question mark, means the words are reworked into another form

explanation.surface: Absolutists stir up trouble at the Soviet news agency Tass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges TASS STIR; Tass was the Soviet news agency, fitting the Russian theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the tsar's autocracy were advocates of absolute monarchy.

clue.text: Plant horse chestnut

definitions.meaning: a sour-leaved herb of the dock family
a reddish-brown horse, a chestnut-coloured horse

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a sour-leaved herb and a reddish-brown horse coat colour.

clue.text: Requiring employment, character means to communicate

parts.note: a post is a job, employment
a card is a character, an amusing eccentric

explanation.surface: A job-seeking eccentric needs a way to get in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: CARD means an eccentric person, as in 'he's a real card'.
explanation.definitionFit: A card mailed with a short message is a way of communicating.

clue.text: Where circus audience is engrossed

definitions.meaning: under the big top, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Intent means absorbed in something, and split in two it places the crowd under canvas.
